classification.difficultyReason: Translate a supplied partial-side ratio to full-side ratios, choose SAS with the common angle and invoke converse angle parallelism; familiar finite proof chain.

content.prompt: The point S is the intersection point of two lines. Points A and B are the intersections of the first line with two other lines, such that B is further away from S than A. Similarly, points C and D are the intersections of the second line with the two other lines, such that D is further away from S than C. Prove that if $SA:AB=SC:CD$, then the two intercepting lines $AC$ and $BD$ are parallel.

spec.description: S-A-B/S-C-D same rays and source order. No parallel arrows or implied equality marks on AC/BD; parallelism is the required conclusion.
spec.mathematics: S-A-B/S-C-D same rays and source order. No parallel arrows or implied equality marks on AC/BD; parallelism is the required conclusion.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens only; no answer values added.

answer.worked: The hypothesis gives $SA\cdot CD=SC\cdot AB$. Add $SA\cdot SC$ to both sides and factor: $SA(SC+CD)=SC(SA+AB)$. Thus $SA\cdot SD=SC\cdot SB$, so $\frac{SA}{SB}=\frac{SC}{SD}$. The included angle ASC is the common angle BSD. Hence $\triangle SAC\sim\triangle SBD$ by SAS. Corresponding angles give $\angle SAC=\angle SBD$, and the converse corresponding-angle property gives $AC\parallel BD$.
